==== Ukraine and white bias ====
Regarding the humanitarian crisis in [[Ukraine]], following the 2022 [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]], Tedros said that the attention given to the conflict was significantly larger than other crises in [[Ethiopia]], [[Yemen]], [[Syria]] or [[Afghanistan]] and said it seemed like this was a result of bias against non-white lives.<ref name=tagbias>{{Cite news |date=13 April 2022 |title=Ukraine attention shows bias against black lives, WHO chief says |language=en-GB |publisher=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-61101732 |access-date=14 April 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=WHO chief: 'Colour of skin' may be why Tigray crisis not getting attention |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/who-chief-colour-skin-may-be-why-tigray-crisis-not-getting-attention-2022-08-17/ |publisher=Reuters |date=17 August 2022}}</ref>

In February 2023, he rejected criticism from the Russian government that the WHO was using the word "invasion" to describe Russia's invasion of Ukraine, saying that "I used the same word in a speech last year. I couldn't find any other word that would represent it because it's the truth."<ref>{{cite news |title=WHO Chief Fires Back in Clash with Russia |url=https://healthpolicy-watch.news/who-chief-fires-back-in-clash-with-russia/ |work=Health Policy Watch |date=4 February 2023}}</ref>

==== Blockade of the Tigray region ====
In early October 2021, [[Mark Lowcock]], who led [[United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs|OCHA]] during part of the [[Tigray War]] between the Ethiopian government and [[Tigray Region|Tigray]] rebels, stated that the Ethiopian federal government was deliberately starving Tigray.<ref>{{cite news | last1= Schifrin | first1= Nick | title= Ethiopia's 'sophisticated campaign' to withhold food, fuel and other aid from Tigray | date= 6 October 2021 |newspaper= [[PBS]] | url= https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/ethiopias-sophisticated-campaign-to-withhold-food-fuel-and-other-aid-from-tigray |access-date= 16 October 2021 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20211016045014/https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/ethiopias-sophisticated-campaign-to-withhold-food-fuel-and-other-aid-from-tigray |archive-date= 16 October 2021 |url-status=live }}</ref> Tedros called the blockade by Ethiopia "an insult to our humanity", saying "Imagine a complete blockade of seven million people for more than a year. And there is no food. There is no medication, no medicine. No electricity. No telecom. No media."<ref>{{cite news |title=Blockade creates 'hell' in Ethiopia's Tigray: WHO |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/1/12/blockade-creates-hell-in-ethiopias-tigray-who |publisher=Al Jazeera English |date=12 January 2022}}</ref>

==== Mpox declaration ====
On 23 July 2022, Tedros declared the [[2022–2023 mpox outbreak|2022 mpox outbreak]] a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC),<ref>{{cite web |title=Second meeting of the International Health Regulations (2005) (IHR) Emergency Committee regarding the multi-country outbreak of monkeypox|url=https://www.who.int/news/item/23-07-2022-second-meeting-of-the-international-health-regulations-(2005)-(ihr)-emergency-committee-regarding-the-multi-country-outbreak-of-monkeypox |publisher=[[World Health Organization]] |access-date=23 July 2022}}</ref> despite 9 of the experts in the committee disagreeing with the call and only 6 in favour.<ref>{{cite news |title=WHO's Tedros acted as tie-breaker to break disagreement over Monkeypox designation|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/whos-tedros-acted-tie-breaker-break-disagreement-over-monkeypox-designation-2022-07-23/ |publisher=[[Reuters]] |date=23 July 2022 |access-date=27 July 2022}}</ref>

===Second term (2022–present)===
====Reelection bid====
[[File:DG Okonjo-Iweala meets with Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus and Daren Tang (53182928629).jpg|thumb|Tedros with [[World Intellectual Property Organization|WIPO]]'s [[Daren Tang]] and [[World Trade Organization|WTO]]'s [[Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala]] in 2023]]
Tedros made plans to seek re-appointment as early as May 2021.<ref name="hbnew">{{cite news |last1=Branswell |first1=Helen |title=WHO's Tedros plans to seek reelection, setting up referendum on his leadership |url=https://www.statnews.com/2021/05/03/tedros-second-term/ |publisher=STAT News |date=3 May 2021}}</ref> On 22 September 2021 Germany proposed him for a further term without opposition.<ref name=denew/> In fact by 29 October he had been nominated by 28 nations: Austria, Bahrain, Barbados, Botswana, Cook Islands, Croatia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Indonesia, Ireland, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Oman, Portugal, Rwanda, Slovakia, Spain, Sweden, Tonga, and Trinidad and Tobago.<ref name=whonew/> He was poised for a second term since no opposing candidate has surfaced.<ref name=denew>{{cite news |title=Tedros seen uncontested for WHO top job after Berlin nod |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210922-tedros-seen-uncontested-for-who-top-job-after-berlin-nod |access-date=22 September 2021 |publisher=[[France24]] |date=22 September 2021}}</ref> He was re-appointed on 24 May 2022,<ref name="tagrenew">{{cite news |title=Tedros re-elected to lead the World Health Organization |url=https://news.un.org/en/story/2022/05/1118952 |work=UN News |date=24 May 2022}}</ref> unopposed for a term that was scheduled to begin on 16 August 2022.<ref name="whonew">{{cite news |title=World Health Organization Secretariat announcement regarding the election of the next WHO Director-General |url=https://www.who.int/news/item/29-10-2021-world-health-organization-secretariat-announcement-regarding-the-election-of-the-next-who-director-general |publisher=World Health Organization |date=29 October 2021}}</ref>

==== Termination of regional director Takeshi Kasai ====
Under Tedros "zero tolerance" policy against misconduct, doctor Takeshi Kasai was dismissed in 2023 from his role as the Western Pacific regional director, the first time in WHO's history for someone at such a high position. An internal investigation had found Kasai to have engaged in public humiliation of staff members and making comments such as the "inferior culture" and "race" of Pacific countries that did not have the capacity to manage COVID-19 cases on their own. Several workers also said Kasai improperly shared sensitive vaccine information to help Japan, his home country. Observers remarked that Tedros needs to enforce the policy more consistently, even in low profile cases such as [[Kivu Ebola epidemic#Sex abuse accusations|reports of sexual abuse and exploitation]] during the 2018–2020 [[Kivu Ebola epidemic]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 March 2023 |title=WHO fires director in Asia accused of racist misconduct |url=https://apnews.com/article/who-asia-racism-misconduct-c01c86cf6bbfe6bec002126e737b4894 |access-date=8 November 2023 |publisher=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref>

==== In office ====
[[File:20.09.2023 - Encontro com o Diretor-Geral da Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS), Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus.jpg|thumb|Tedros with Brazilian President [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]] in September 2023]]
In February 2023, following the [[2023 Turkey–Syria earthquakes|Turkey–Syria earthquakes]], Ghebreyesus visited [[Antakya]], Turkey, and [[Aleppo]], Syria, to ensure more aid to the affected areas.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/turkey-syria-earthquake-who-chief-arrives-3271571 |title=WHO chief arrives in Syria's quake-hit Aleppo: State media |publisher=Channel NewsAsia |date=11 February 2023 |archive-date=11 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230211132157/https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/turkey-syria-earthquake-who-chief-arrives-3271571 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=WHO's Tedros pledges support after first visit to Turkey's quake zone |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/whos-tedros-pledges-support-after-first-visit-turkeys-quake-zone-2023-02-28/ |publisher=Reuters |date=28 February 2023}}</ref>

In 2023, he warned of the [[Humanitarian impact of the war in Sudan (2023)|humanitarian impact]] of the [[War in Sudan (2023)|war in Sudan]], saying that 40% of the Sudanese population was suffering from hunger.<ref>{{cite news |title=Over 40% of Sudanese people suffer from hunger: WHO chief |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/over-40-of-sudanese-people-suffer-from-hunger-who-chief/2964670 |publisher=[[Anadolu Agency]] |date=9 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=WHO Sounds Warning On Sudan Health Crisis |url=https://www.barrons.com/news/who-sounds-warning-on-sudan-health-crisis-40ba6a7b |work=Barron's |date=29 December 2023}}</ref>

In December 2023, speaking about the situation in [[Afghanistan]], Ghebreyesus said that 30% of the [[Demographics of Afghanistan|Afghan population]] was [[Aftermath of the Afghanistan War (2001–2021)#Humanitarian crisis|facing acute food insecurity]], adding that "Close to 1 million children are severely malnourished and 2.3 million are suffering from moderate acute malnutrition. WHO needs $ 185 million to continue providing medicine and supporting hospitals to prevent more Afghan children and women from dying of malnutrition and the consequences of food insecurity."<ref>{{cite news |title=Over 1 mn Afghan children facing severe malnutrition, says WHO chief |url=https://www.business-standard.com/world-news/over-1-mn-afghan-children-facing-severe-malnutrition-says-who-chief-123122200080_1.html |work=Business Standard |date=22 December 2023}}</ref>

In October 2025, Tedros condemned the [[El Fasher massacre]] in [[Sudan]], including the reported killings of over 460 patients and companions at the Saudi Maternity Hospital in [[El Fasher]].<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Shelton |first1=Joe |last2=Connor |first2=Richard |date=29 October 2025 |title=Sudan: WHO 'appalled' by RSF maternity ward massacre |url=https://www.dw.com/en/sudan-who-appalled-by-rsf-maternity-ward-massacre/a-74537649?maca=en-rss-en-africa-8291-rdf |access-date=29 October 2025 |work=[[Deutsche Welle]] |language=en }}</ref>

==== Gaza war ====
{{Further|Gaza war}}
Tedros condemned the attack by [[Hamas]] on [[Israel]] on 7 October 2023 and called for the release of all [[Gaza war hostage crisis|hostages]].<ref>{{cite news |title=WHO chief urges Hamas to free hostages |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/who-chief-urges-hamas-to-free-hostages/article67424689.ece |work=The Hindu |date=16 October 2023}}</ref>

On 29 October 2023, Tedros described as "deeply concerning" reports from the Palestinian Red Crescent that the [[al-Quds hospital]] had received an urgent [[2023 Gaza Strip evacuations|evacuation warning]] and notice that it was "going to be bombarded" as "deeply concerning." He reiterated that it was "impossible to evacuate hospitals full of patients without endangering their lives".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2023/oct/29/israel-hamas-war-live-netanyahu-declares-offensives-second-stage-gaza-internet-coming-back-online?page=with:block-653e4a1a8f0837aa4c22d148#block-653e4a1a8f0837aa4c22d148 |title=Israel-Hamas war live: WHO 'deeply concerned' by report of evacuation warning to Gaza's al-Quds hospital |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=29 October 2023 |last1=Lowe |first1=Yohannes |last2=Hall |first2=Rachel |last3=Ratcliffe |first3=Rebecca |archive-date=29 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231029132131/https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2023/oct/29/israel-hamas-war-live-netanyahu-declares-offensives-second-stage-gaza-internet-coming-back-online?page=with%3Ablock-653e4a1a8f0837aa4c22d148#block-653e4a1a8f0837aa4c22d148 |url-status=live}}</ref> He said on X that he was "utterly shocked by reports of attacks on ambulances evacuating patients", adding that patients, health workers and medical facilities must always be protected.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/health-ministry-gaza-says-israel-targeted-convoy-ambulances-leaving-al-shifa-2023-11-03/ |title=Israel strikes ambulance near Gaza hospital, 15 reported killed |publisher=[[Reuters]] |archive-date=3 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231103235417/https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/health-ministry-gaza-says-israel-targeted-convoy-ambulances-leaving-al-shifa-2023-11-03/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

In December 2023, he criticized Israel's [[2023 Israeli blockade of the Gaza Strip|blockade of the Gaza Strip]], saying that "Resupplying health facilities has become extremely difficult and is deeply compromised by the security situation on the ground and inadequate resupply from outside Gaza."<ref>{{cite news |title=WHO adopts resolution to address 'catastrophic' health situation in Gaza |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/who-resolution-catastrophic-health-gaza-1.7054852 |publisher=CBC News |date=10 December 2023}}</ref>

In January 2024, Tedros described conditions in Gaza as "hellish". He called for a ceasefire and a "true solution" to the Israel-Palestinian conflict.<ref>{{cite news |title=WHO chief breaks down describing 'hellish' Gaza conditions |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/who-chief-breaks-down-describing-hellish-gaza-conditions-2024-01-25/ |publisher=Reuters |date=26 January 2024}}</ref>

On 26 December 2024, Tedros was caught up in an [[26 December 2024 Israeli attack on Yemen|Israeli airstrike]] on [[Sanaa International Airport]] in Yemen while he was visiting the country on official business.<ref>{{cite news |title=UN health chief at Yemen airport during Israeli strikes |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clyj88rye1jo |publisher=BBC News |date=27 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Tawfeeq |first1=Mohammed |last2=Salem |first2=Mostafa |last3=Nasser |first3=Irene |title=WHO chief and UN team caught up in Israeli strikes that killed six in Yemen |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2024/12/26/middleeast/israeli-strikes-yemen-sanaa-houthis-intl/index.html |publisher=CNN |date=26 December 2024 |language=en}}</ref> He later developed [[tinnitus]] from the explosions.<ref>{{cite news |title=WHO director urges Israel to stop attacks on Gaza's medical infrastructure |url=https://www.npr.org/2024/12/31/nx-s1-5242471/israel-gaza-ceasefire-health-crisis |publisher=NPR |date=31 December 2024}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Tedros is married and has five children.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/health-40010522 |title=Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus: Ethiopian wins top WHO job |date=23 May 2017|publisher=[[BBC News]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170627123024/http://www.bbc.com/news/health-40010522 |archive-date=27 June 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> He is an [[Ethiopian Orthodox Christian]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://m.facebook.com/permalink.php?story_fbid=552442938158536&id=544913925578104 | title=Facebook | via=[[Facebook]] }}{{User-generated source|certain=yes|date=May 2022}}</ref>

==Membership==

* 2005–2009: Partnership for Maternal, Newborn & Child Health, co-chair<ref name=2013-PMNCH-CoChair>{{cite web|title=Note for the Record –PMNCH Executive Committee Teleconference|url=https://www.who.int/pmnch/about/steering_committee/2009_10_13_nfr.pdf|publisher=Partnership for Maternal, Newborn & Child Health (PMNCH)|date=13 October 2013|access-date=7 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131030084603/http://www.who.int/pmnch/about/steering_committee/2009_10_13_nfr.pdf|archive-date=30 October 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>
